newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil not worried by B Band court injunction.
newsitem.headline: Brazil not worried by B Band court injunction.

text.p: A Brazilian judge has granted an injunction to halt the privatization of one of 10 B Band cellular concessions, but the government said the process continues and the ruling would be overturned.
"There's nothing to be concerned about," said Francisco Mendonca, a Communications Ministry spokesman.

The injunction, granted by a federal judge in the northeastern state of Pernambuco, calls for the government to "stop the judging process for choosing a winner" for concession area No. 10, Mendonca told Reuters.
The area comprises the states of Alagoas, Ceara, Paraiba, Pernambuco, Piaui and Rio Grande do Norte states.
Mendonca said the government has not halted its work as a result of the injunction because actual analysis of proposals for the area has not begun yet.

"We're still in the process of officially receiving the qualification documents. The analysis won't start for another week and a half," he said, adding that gives the government "plenty of time" to overturn the injunction.
The government put to tender a total of 10 cellular B Band concession areas on Monday and received bids from 15 consortia on all but one.
Mendonca said similar injunctions were tossed out before the auction and expressed confidence the same fate awaited Wednesday's decision by federal Judge Edwiges Wanderley.
Local newspapers said the government plans to seek the overturning of the injunction, which was sought by the Telecommunications Workers Union in Pernambuco.
